acceptanceCriteria: One corvint-mcp process serves several repositories that the operator declares at startup (repeated --root or a roots file, each with a short alias); authority still comes only from operator startup arguments, never from client roots or request data (MCPV0-015 intent preserved).

Every repository-scoped tool takes a required repository alias when more than one root is declared; an unknown or missing alias is refused with a stable code; one declared root keeps today's single-root bytes and conformance vectors unchanged.
The tool list is sent once regardless of repository count; measured tools/list bytes and process count for 1, 3 and 10 roots are recorded against today's one-server-per-repo setup.
Repository bindings open lazily on first call, at most a bounded number stay open (least-recently-used close), and an idle server does no background work.
Each result stays bound to its own repository and revision identity (invariant 1); results from different roots never mix.
An accepted multi-root authority profile spec amends MCPV0-001/MCPV0-015 before implementation is called done; the same option is evaluated for the test-validity, docs and corpus servers.
Maintained tests cover alias routing, refusal of undeclared roots, the bounded open set, and single-root byte parity.
body:
Filed 2026-10-07 by the orchestrator session from an owner request: when several repositories are in use, agents run one Corvint MCP server per repository, and the owner asked to combine them into one server that routes to each repository.

Today MCPV0-001 makes corvint-mcp own exactly one --root, and MCPV0-015 says multi-root support later requires an accepted multi-root authority profile. So N repositories mean N processes and N copies of the same tool schemas in every agent turn.

Orchestrator recommendation: in-process multi-root routing in corvint-mcp, not a proxy that spawns one child per root (a proxy keeps N processes and adds lifecycle and error-forwarding work). Expected saving: tool-schema tokens drop from N times to once per turn; measured numbers come from the token-usage audit and the acceptance measurement. Spec acceptance is human-owned.

title: corvint-mcp: serve several operator-declared repositories from one MCP server instead of one server per repository
